messages:
sam (support): FYI customer ACME (acct: acme-inc) reporting a sharp p99 jump after yesterday's model swap to the new tokenizer variant. p95 ~230ms -> 450ms, p99 420ms -> 1.6s. first seen ~09:12 UTC. ticket #INC-12345. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/graphs/shot?p=acme

mike (runtime): linking the deploy - we rolled tokenizer/merge v2 at 03:50 UTC yesterday. any errors in logs?

ashok (mlinfra): pulling kvcache and decode times now. initial glance: kvcache_miss_rate up ~3x for requests >8k tokens. also seeing increased tokenization time on extended contexts.

julia (eng): can we get a minimal repro? customer says long prompts (8k-12k) and intermittent 504s.

sam (support): repro snippet customer provided (redacted):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"mistral-lite-v2-tokenized","input": "<8k prompt>...<4k more>"}'
```
Response times vary wildly. They attached a few raw request_ids: req_20240312_01, req_20240312_05. Logs show repeated `decode` spikes: 
```
[2024-03-12T09:12:05Z] req=req_20240312_05 decode_ms=1200 total_ms=1650 kvcache_hit=false
[2024-03-12T09:12:05Z] req=req_20240312_05 trace=tokenizer:430ms decode:1200ms
```

eng-oncall-bot: alert 4521: p99_latency > 1s for model=mistral-lite-v2-tokenized in prod-us-east-1 (since 09:10 UTC).

ashok (mlinfra): hypothesis: tokenizer merge changed byte-align normalization and increased per-token overhead for non-ASCII sequences; combined with cold KVCache population for very long contexts leads to decode blowup. kvcache warmup previously amortized by different tokenization boundaries.

mike (runtime): agreed. also the runtime kernel selection logic has a threshold at seq_len=2048 that picks a slow path for kvcache population. If token boundaries shift we may push more requests onto the slow path.

carol (support-lead): customer is on a revenue-sensitive flow; they want ETA. are there quick mitigations we can apply now?

julia (eng): yes -- options: 1) roll back to previous tokenizer variant for that customer or global until fix, 2) route long-context requests to fallback model (mistral-lite-v1) for this account, 3) enable temporary request-size gating/batching so we don't hit the slow decode path concurrently.

sam (support): they asked for a rollback ASAP. they can tolerate a model mismatch for a short window.

mike (runtime): I'm starting a scoped rollback for account acme-inc -> switching model mapping to v1 via routing rule. will also increase max concurrent workers on the nodes handling their traffic while rollback executes.

ashok (mlinfra): parallel: I'll create a short repro harness (long sequence synthetic) and run on perf nodes to validate. adding metric `kvcache_warmup_ms` and a tag for tokenizer_variant.

julia (eng): for longer term: we should adjust kernel selection heuristics to be robust to token boundary shifts, and add unit perf tests for tokenizer-normalization differences on long context. file a follow-up PR for evals.

sam (support): noted. I've updated ticket #INC-12345: mitigation=route->v1, rollback_initiated_by=@mike, eta ~5m. customer pinged and accepts workaround.

mike (runtime): rollback finished, routing rule active. monitoring shows p99 back to ~480ms for that account. global p99 for model still high because some traffic not routed; continuing to watch.

eng-oncall-bot: alert resolved (4521) at 09:26 UTC based on p99 window.

carol (support-lead): great. next steps: asahok to push perf repro, julia to spec kernel heuristics, mike to prepare safer rollout checklist for tokenizer merges (canary on long-context queries). sam to follow up with customer and close when stable.

sam (support): will send summary and escalate to product for rollout policy changes. closing interim ticket note. :white_check_mark:
